newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia Gas Commission rolls back rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia Gas Commission rolls back rate hike.

text.p: The Philadelphia Gas Commission voted Tuesday to roll back by two percent an interim increase in the Gas Cost Rate which took effect Oct 1, 1996.

At its meeting September 24, 1996, the Gas Commission approved PGW's request for an interim increase in the GCR in the amount of $1.6517 to offset PGW's forecasted $23 million increase in gas costs during fiscal 1997 and its under-collection from fiscal 1996.

The Gas Commission, following its evaluation of the forecasted gas costs and testimony from public hearings, approved a GCR of approximately $1.40 per mcf which will result in a $15 to $20 savings per year for the average household from the interim GCR approved September 24.

The Gas Commission is required by city ordinance to review and approve PGW rates and charges, including the GCR, before they can become effective. The GCR is designed to pass through to the ratepayers fluctuations in the cost of gas supplies.
The new interim GCR will take effect December 1, 1996.
